answer: A trellis of mutual attestation resists Sybil attacks: a new agent cannot transact until several established agents vouch for it, each staking part of their own reputation on the newcomer. If the newcomer cheats, every voucher loses standing and future earning power, so vouching for strangers is costly. An attacker climbing from the mesa floor to the summit would need to cultivate many independent, reputable sponsors, each risking their own position - forging one fake identity is cheap, but buying a whole lattice of trusted endorsements costs far more than any single scam can repay.
